children: S&P expects Adani Ports' debt-to-Ebitda ratio to remain below its 3.5 times downside threshold despite the acquisition

Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) is expected to absorb the financial impact of its proposed acquisition of Netherlands-based Evos BV without a significant deterioration in its credit profile, according to S&P Global Ratings.

The acquisition, valued at an enterprise value of €2.56 billion (approximately Rs 27,000 crore), is expected to expand Adani Ports' international footprint while strengthening its presence in the storage and handling of transition fuels.

S&P expects the company's adjusted debt-to-Ebitda ratio to reach 2.3 times in FY28 and 2.7 times in FY29. Both projections remain below the rating agency's downside threshold of 3.5 times, indicating that the acquisition is unlikely to exert significant pressure on its credit metrics.
The acquisition of Evos will expand Adani Ports' presence in Europe and diversify its business beyond conventional port operations.

Evos operates terminals for the storage and handling of liquid bulk products, including fuels and chemicals. The acquisition will also give Adani Ports greater exposure to transition fuels such as biofuels, methanol and sustainable aviation fuel.
The deal is expected to strengthen the company's position in the global energy supply chain as demand for alternative fuels and related infrastructure develops.
Evos is projected to contribute around 9 per cent of Adani Ports' total Ebitda in FY29, according to S&P's assessment.
The earnings contribution is expected to support the company's financial performance as it integrates the acquired business into its existing portfolio.
S&P's assessment suggests that Adani Ports has sufficient financial flexibility to undertake the acquisition while keeping leverage within the rating agency's stated thresholds.

The acquisition also marks a further step in the company's strategy to expand its international operations and diversify its revenue base through investments in global logistics and energy infrastructure.
